properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/09/2026 to COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/09/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8280933
Permit API: 083-47442
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/09/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Chuck Rippey of Copperhead Enterprises on 7/8/26 of a crude oil spill due to a compromised subsurface gathering line located at the entrance of the spur road that accesses this conventional well. At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2023 to RECLUSIVE ENERGY LLC in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RECLUSIVE ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2023
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 998675
Permit API: 083-47406
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/15/2023
Comments: This was an inspection performed following a report that the operator had a leaking brine tank on the Enis Lease. I inspected all three tank batteries on this lease.This well is producing and is equipped with a gas powered pumpjack. No spills or leaks are noted at the well. There is a tank battery near the well with two 210 barrel stock tanks contained. There is a buried brine tank across the access road in a wooded area. It appears that there has been an ongoing small leak in the tank, which has allowed brine to leak out into the soil. Impacted soil is apparent ~35 linear feet from the tank, at the base of a small hill. A check with a soil EC meter showed conductivity ranging from 1.5 to 5 mS in the soil. The liquid, along with deer activity, has stripped away vegetation from a 10x15 foot area. The water does not appear to have traveled much further than this and does not appear to be a threat to enter the waters of the Commonwealth.After this visit, I called the operator and he came to the site a little later to look at it with me. He agreed that the tank appeared to be leaking. I suggested that the tank would need to be vacuumed out, removed from the ground and the impacted soils remediated. He said that he would be contacting a contractor immediately to begin this process. Continued followup will be done as necessary.

Inspection Type: Routine/Partial/Aerial Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2022
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on (5) of the (6) wells on the Cappucci pad. The Cappucci 4H, N 2H, 102H, N 4H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. The 2H is not involved in todays Pressure Build Up Tests. This is the 2nd round of SPBUTs since remedial Perf. and Squeeze work performed on the Cappucci 4H, N 2H and the 102H was completed on 6/14/22. SPBUTs were initiated on 11/28/22 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The (20x13) annulus was shut in on 11/28/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 96 hrs - The progressive shut in for the (13x9) annulus was missed on 11/29/22, resulting in a 96 hr shut in for the (20x13) annulus - The (13x9) annulus was shut in on 11/30/22 @ ~ 09:50 - 48 hrs - The (9x5) annulus was shut in on 12/1/22 @ ~ 11:00 - 24 hrs - All (6) wells annuli were shut in at time of sampling. - Upon arrival I met with Creston Consultants reps. Jason Rajan and Dakota Manning and CALLC rep. Patrick Gardner. Starting at approx. 11:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resources' DeCristo (01-128) D well site located in Sullivan Township, Bradford County on 9/16/2025 at 1115 hours. The weather was 69 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported discovered release. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #392245 is tied to the release within CTS.The eight active well permits and erosion and sediment control general permit currently list Seneca Resources (Seneca) as the operator. Repsol Oil and Gas (Repsol) is currently handling overlook of some operations during flowback, including the offloading and transportation of produced water from the site. Seneca and Repsol are currently working on transferring the permits back to Repsol. On 9/15/2025, Repsol contacted the DEP to report that during screening efforts prior to transferring the permits back to Repsol, a consultant (WSP) discovered an area on the pad surface where a suspected release of produced water occurred. The suspected release was discovered on 9/12/2025. Repsol reported that the release quantity was unknown but calculations determined that the release was likely more than a barrel. The release was determined to be located in front of the produced water tanks' offload area and was spread linearly across the pad surface towards the "exit" of the pad (photos #2 and 3). Since the site's and wells' permits are currently under Seneca ownership, I recommended that Seneca report the release to the DEP. Seneca contacted the DEP reporting hotline on 9/15/2025 to report the discovery of the suspected release on behalf of Seneca. Seneca reported that the exact time of the release was unknown but is assumed to have occurred during flowback. The suspected release was discovered due to elevated electrical conductivity readings noted during the pad assessment which was conducted by WSP.During today's inspection, it was observed that the release had already been remediated. No evidence of any spills/releases was observed. The areas remediated have already been backfilled and were dry today (photos #2 and 3). Based on the reported discovery of a release of an unknown quantity outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22244 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed the site at 1245 hours.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 8/20/2025 at 0830 hours. The weather was 62 degrees F with rain. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.No remediation excavation activities were occurring today due to the rain. Impacted materials stored within secondary containment (photo #2) continue to be loaded into trucks and hauled offsite for disposal. An interceptor trench was installed around the entire secondary containment on the pad surface that collects fluids and diverts them into a pipe (photo #1) that eventually flows into the trench below the pad's fill slope. Fluids were flowing into the lined detention basin from both the eastern and western lined channels today (photos #5 and 6). Fluids flowing in the western channel were field measured at ~6mS/cm and fluids flowing the in the eastern channel were field measured at ~370us/cm. Less than 6 inches of fluids were currently held in the lined detention basin (photo #4).Resource Environmental collected samples from the three shallow, monitoring wells drilled downslope of the well pad on 8/7/2025. Repsol reported that the samples collected on 8/7/2025 from Monitoring Well (MW) MW04A showed that elevated constituents were reported. MW04A can be seen in photo #10 and is located downslope of the preexisting stormwater basin. During remediation of the preexisting stormwater basin, a large rock was removed and a ~4-inch borehole was discovered beneath the basin (photo #9). Repsol reported that the borehole was ~27 feet deep and was not discovered during construction because it is located on the fill side of the basin and was ~3 feet beneath the native soils. It is unclear at this time if the borehole is causing the elevated constituents found in MW04A. Resource Environmental continues weekly sampling from the three shallow, monitoring wells, streams and various seeps on the fill slope. Repsol intends to have confirmatory samples collected from the soils in the remediated stormwater basin, and then backfill, however, a permanent structure will be installed to allow continued access to the discovered borehole. Resource Environmental was screening and purging fluids from the borehole today. Shallow, monitoring well MW01A has not been drilled yet. A rig is tentatively scheduled for drilling of MW01A and the four deep monitoring wells sometime next week. A puddle within the remediated basin (photo #8) returned a field measured reading of ~360us/cm.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-01 to Msl Oil & Gas Corp in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Msl Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-01
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 883843
Permit API: 083-47035
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-01
Comments: Brian Ayers of DEP was contacted by MSL's Dick Pascarella on 4/23/2020 regarding a condensate leak from a tank that was found that day. PA Fish and Boat Commission officer Tom Mcmann was on site 4/24/2020 to follow up and took some photos that are included in this report. It appears as though a small, uncontained drip gas tank had a failure at a fitting at some point prior to the spill being found. This tank holds mostly water that condenses from the gas coming from the compressor station nearby, but also contains some condensed petroleum liquids. An estimated 5-10 gallons of this fluid escaped from the broken fitting and was spilled to the ground. Some of this ran down slope toward an UNT of Chappel Fork, with some collecting in a low, wet area and a small amount eventually entering the water. Tom Mcmann documented photos of the condensate in the vernal pool area, which is included in the attached photos. A Department site visit was performed 5/1/2020. The operator has scraped up the surface of the contaminated site, and placed down straw mulch and seed. They also put down gravel around equipment close to the stream and have built containment around the drip gas tank. The area close to the stream was observed to have a strong condensate odor and some sheen could be spotted entering the stream when this area was agitated on the stream banks. Some product was noted, mostly in the form of sheen, in the UNT Chappel Fork. The stream crosses Chappel Fork Rd a few feet from where the product entered, and sheen was visible upon agitation approximately 150-200 feet downstream. No free product was apparent and no other waters were impacted. The operator was contacted and instructed to place booms for containment and monitor through the weekend, followed by a run of agitating the stream bottom to push any product caught in the substrate to collect it in the next week. They also dug up the impacted soil next to the stream with shovels and removed it. Bill Otto of MSL sent photos to show that booms were placed and digging done as of late Friday, May 1. Further followup will be done as possible.

Report Details

Violation Date: 11/18/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8208628
Permit API: 081-21708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/18/2024
Comments: On November 18, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a incident response inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Elbow Fish and Game Club Pad C. On November 16, 2024, Rick Hall with EQT notified the DEP spill hotline, it was reported that a line from a water truck failed. DEP spoke with Rick Hall on the phone and he informed DEP that a seal on a lubricator for a swabbing rig failed and sprayed about 5 gallons of produced fluid onto the well pad surface. The sprayed production fluid impacted an area of approximately 41 ft. by 18 ft. EQT had contractors onsite excavate the impacted soil and put it in a dumpster. When DEP arrived, the area of excavation had been backfilled with clean fill. There were no areas of staining or pooled watered near by. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.There are a total of 7 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. The wells have separators in line with them. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the well cellars was observed. There are 7 GPUs and 4 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both the GPUs and production fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment. One dehydration unit is located onsite in containment.Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted but the violations were immediately corrected.

Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8275604

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 5/18/2026
Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4180049.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. The stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection. The rig has been removed from the site at this time. The well head is observed in the well cellar.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plan is on site. The E and S plan has not been updated to depict the stream that runs under the access road. - Plastic matting has been removed from all three locations along the access road and from on site. - Disturbance along the access road is observed in multiple areas which appears to be due to vehicle traffic (Photos 4-8, 11-14). The Department recommends the operator repair the disturbance during site restoration.- Sedimentation observed in previous inspection remains visible along the access road above the culvert outlet (Photo 9). The Department recommends the operator return the sediment to the access road and install E and S BMPs above the culvert to prevent sedimentation to the stream channel. - The stream channel (Photo 10) appears to be dry at this time. - The timber mat bridge at the site entrance appears to have been removed (Photo 15).- CFS on the well site appears to be improperly implemented/maintained in two areas (Photos 16-17). The Department recommends the operator ensure CFS is staked with no more than 10 feet between each stake. - Soil stockpile is osberved to be experiencing some vegetative growth on the back side (Photo 20).- Well cellar is observed and well tag/posting requirements are met on site. - Pump jack remains on site at this time. Violations are being continued for failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, failure to identify a stream on the E and S plan, failure to implement/maintain E and S BMPs, and accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road. Violations were also continued in IR 4201247 for staining still observed near twp previously observed minor releases of petroleum products and/or brine.

It appears additional material has been excavated in the ditch up to the northern and southern booms as well as around the production equipment. There appeared to be a large amount of excavation where the production tank previously was, with excavation appearing reach approximately 4 feet deep. These readings appear to be comparable to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.16mS. The Department recommends the operator promptly install/implement temporary erosion and sediment controls. The Department also recommends the operator temporarily stabilize any disturbed areas with in 4 days following cessation of earth disturbance activities. Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

Comments: On 11/30/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Stech F69 well. The following was observed:The well and operator's information were posted onsite (Photos 1, 2).The wellhead, production equipment, and production tank were in generally good condition. Some corrosion noted, loose wires/equipment near wellhead (Photos 3-6). Tank fluids high - I recommend pumping fluid out and placing lid on tank (Photo 7).Silt fence in the woods below production tank. I recommend ensuring that no sediment from the site washes downslope towards the tributary below (Photo 8).The access road was in poor condition leading the whole way to the site from the main road (Photos 9-25 with specific locations). Several areas displayed lack of maintenence and drainage concerns seen by pooling, potholes, channelization, and accelerated erosion. Culverts that run under the road leading to tributary to Pigeon Creek appeared to require clean out and outlet protection - erosion at outlets. There was a section of the access road closer to the entrance gate that displayed undercutting and failure along the guardrail. The integrity of the access road appeared jeopardized and may progress with repeated rain events and heavy truck traffic. The road does not display a safe way for emergency vehicles to navigate in case of emergency at the wellsite.Observations communicated to operator via phone on 11/30/23.Due to the poor condition of the access road and lack of maintenance, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78.53, and 102.22(a)2ii are being issued.

Comments: Weather: Warm, 85 degrees F, humid, slight wind. I arrived to the location at 1110 on 7/1/2022. Brian Bowers (Company Man) accompanied me during the inspection. Seneca plans to stimulate a total of 7 gas wells (e.g. 1 Marcellus and 6 Utica) located on the Cruttenden 846 pad over the next several weeks. Stimulation began at the pad on 6/17/2022. At the time of the inspection, Halliburton completed Stage 22 of 70 at the Cruttenden 31HU and Stage 32 of 80 at the Cruttenden 32HU; they were actively stimulating Stage 16 of 65 at the Cruttenden 33HU and were perforating Stage 23 of 70 at the Cruttenden 31HU. They are currently zipper fracing the Cruttenden 31HU, 32HU, and 33HU, which are Utica wells. Gas samples were collected from all 3 annuli at the Cruttenden 32HU at the conclusion of a pressure build-up test on 5/2/2022 (Inspection Record #3356904). Isotopic results confirmed the presence of combustible gas, primarily methane, at all 3 annuli. As a result, a violation of 78a.85(a)(5) was cited during an administrative inspection conducted on 5/26/2022 (Inspection Record #3368592); this is a continuing violation. No new violations were noted during this inspection. I left the location at 1155.

Report Details

Inspection Date: 1/21/2026
Comments: On 1/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 18 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade and vegetated.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Toe preps were conducted last week to open the sleeves of each well. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Mark expects stimulation activities to start the first or second week of February, depending when the crew completes stimulation activities at a different pad. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected. I did witness a secondary containment measuring 6' x 6' with a valve connecting two pipes in it that had liquid in the containment that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The pipe connects the east production tank to one of the frac tanks on the west side of the pad. There was visible evidence of a release of material that overtopped the secondary containment structure. The release was observed in a frozen state, on the unprotected ground in an area measuring approximately 18" x 36" x 0.5" deep. I reported this to Mark who will contact production to have it cleaned.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1300 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Greylock Prod Llc

Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 877367
Permit API: 059-27910
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: On 2/14/20 an incident inspection of the Beacon well pad was conducted in response to a spill (CTS ID: 347983) reported on 2/10/20. The following was observed: >>On 2/11/20 WQSS John Carson spoke with Greylock Representative Keith Eighmey who reported that while drilling using a filming agent foam from an open topped tank blew to the well pad and via a failed seam in the pad containment traveled to the pad's drainage ditches and then to the primary sediment basin and into the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC; unnamed tributary to Frosty Run). The amount of material lost was reported as unknown but minimal. Operator sampling and MSDS were requested. >>At the time of inspection the sediment basin was found to be overflowing via the stand pipe resulting in substantial flow of sediment laden waters bypassing and flowing through site perimeter controls causing accelerated erosion and impact to the WOC. Additionally, the runoff stream and channel off site notably still bore multiple large piles of foam strongly indicating ongoing impact related to the reported spill. At the time of inspection dewatering/pumping out the impacted water from the sediment basin and appropriate disposal of the effluent as site waste was encouraged. Obstruction of the waterway was not approved. This spill and its impact constitutes a violation of 35 P.S. § 6018.301, 35 P.S. § 691.307(a), * 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), 25 Pa. Code § 102.5(m)4, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e), 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1, 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)1, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.53 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. Violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e) and 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1 were related to the failure of site secondary containment and were shown to have been corrected by the operator prior to the time of inspection. >>A concurrent general surface inspection related to the site ESCGP (ESX16-059-0038) was conducted in response to observed site conditions, particularly multiple slope failures.

This barite/water mixture was released directly to the surface of the well pad. No run-off was observed off the well pad. I observed the release area during the inspection and conducted field screen readings for conductivity in the release area. Soil conductivity screening was conducted in the excavated release area. Conductivity field screenings were conducted on the impacted soils; readings ranged from 0.15-0.32 mS/cm. Violations noted. Please note that the cited violations were immediately corrected by the operator after the released occurred.

Violation ID: 8153783
Permit API: 123-44864
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/27/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559).¿¿ ¿¿ ¿¿ The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures.¿¿ As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes approximately 1-2 feet from the well head were placed into the ground to identify if any methane was migrating from the well bore.¿¿All valves are open and the well is currently equipped for production. Two check valves were in place in the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well I.D. needs updated. We were unable to collect a gas sample from the ground at the time of the inspection. Casing pressure was 4 P.S.I. and the tubing pressure was 0 P.S.I. ¿¿ Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. ¿¿ 7%, 15%, and 3% Methane by volume was detected in the three slam bar holes utilizing an MSA ALTAIR 5X Meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. As a result the following violations are being issued against this well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator. OGI Adam Hartle assisted in this inspection.

Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. ¿¿ VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. ¿¿ VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times. The operator hired a third party to remediate the release in accordance with Act 2 standards and this consultant is anticipated to be on-site tomorrow to begin this process. Violations are being issued for this reportable release of fluids.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8246613
Permit API: 015-23610
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/28/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Cahill" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP yesterday (August 27, 2025) to report they discovered an underground flow line leaked an unknown quantity of produced liquid.I spoke with Mike Deming (Expand) on site during this inspection who explained their Forward Looking Infrared (FLIR) camera technician discovered natural gas emitting from the pad surface on Friday August 22, 2025 during a quarterly inspection. On Monday August 25, 2025 Expand pressurized all 3 Marcellus wells with natural gas. The 2H Marcellus well lost approximately 500 psi over 20 minutes, indicating the leak. On Wednesday August 27, 2025 they pressurized the 2H well with air to locate the production line leaks more accurately. Expand checked the fill slope for signs of seepage, and did not see any liquid or stressed vegetation.I spoke with Andy Senefelder (Crescent Environmental, P.G.) on site who explained that yesterday an excavator dug a ~3' deep x ~90' long trench above the production lines. Then they hand dug 9 test pits ("potholes") in the pea gravel surrounding the production line to find the extent of the leaks. Liquid in the potholes returned electrical conductivity (EC) readings of 23-106 mS/cm. Crescent tested the pad material removed for the trench which returned EC readings of 0.05-0.45 mS/cm, indicating the material above the line is not impacted. So far, a vac truck has removed approximately 2 barrels of liquid from sumps in the trench. Demming calculated the approximate maximum amount of liquid released is 21.5 barrels.Expand removed the 2 sections of 4" diameter line that leaked, and are testing the metal to determine a cause of the pinholes in it. They plan to replace all of the production lines between the wells and the GPUs with above ground pipe.After the old lines are removed, Crescent plans to sample in compliance with Act 2 Cleanup standards.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion orsedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Runoff water flows to basins on the east and south ends of the site.Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles on the east end of the pad surface has EC of 0.30-0.55 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5. I did not see any other puddles on the pad.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 2H well permit.Air temp 54FJLP

According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance. However, the RCE is partially laden with sediment at the time of inspection. Additional sediment was observed in the neighboring residential yard and on Jobes Drive. The sediment observed on Jobes Drive appeared to be tracked approximately 150 feet from the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE). Significant tire rutting was observed in the neighboring residential yard and in the access road. The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is available on site.Upon arriving to the well plugging site, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart. Lockhart cautioned the Department that high-pressure lines are active around the gas well, and suggested against approaching the plugging rig during this inspection. Therefore, the area surrounding the well plugging rig was not evaluated during this inspection due to the hazards present.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE), the tire rutting in the access road, the sediment tracked onto Jobes Drive, and for conducting plugging operations in a manner that causes a public nuisance.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: On 12/03/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 30F and snowing. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).The recently drilled wells onsite are currently undergoing stimulation activities (photo #2); the well permits and secondary containment inspection logs are availbe for review in the company man's trailer (photos #3 and 4).This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Greylock personnel on 12/03/2024 at 0115 hours. The report detailed a release of approximately 20 barrels of produced fluids onto the pad-wide secondary containment system; the released fluids accumulated at a low point of the containment system and an approximate 2 barrels of produced fluids escaped from the containment system and onto the pad surface. See CTS #: 385569 for more details.Greylock personnel met with me on site to discuss how the release happened and ongoing remediation efforts. Personnel from Penn E and R were also onsite conducting soil sampling in accordance with an Act 2 remediation plan. By the time I arrived, released fluids were already recovered and contaminated soils were being excavated and removed (photos #5 and 6). Soil screening was being conducted as material was removed to ensure that all contaminated soil is recovered. I also screened soils for electrical conductivity (EC) of the affected area; the area field measured for EC at a range of ~1.40 - >4.00mS/cm (photos #7-9).Fluids on the pad surface drain into an infiltration basin which serves as the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #10). Greylock personnel had already screened the water draining into the infiltration basin but requested that I also screen it to confirm their results. Water entering the infiltration basin field measured for EC at ~0.54mS/cm; this field measurement was consistent with Greylock's (photo #11).Hydraulic fracturing activities continue onsite (photo #12). Numerous brine, sand, temporary storage tanks/containers are noted and are held on containment (photos #13-15). The site's chemical storage area is located on containment, tidy, and all containers are labeled (photo #16). Production equipment and produced fluids tanks have been installed onsite and are to be put into use when the completed wells go into production (photo #17).Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #: 105-21962:- 35 P.S. 691.402(b)- 25 PA 78a.57(a)- 35 P.S. 6018.301The DEP recommends that Greylock proceeds with Act 2 remediation regarding the aforementioned release.I departed the site at 1200 hours.

Violation ID: 893203
Permit API: 027-21534
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 08/31/2020
Comments: Follow-up site inspection on August 31, 2020 at ARD's COP Tract 231 well pad. Prior to my site inspection I spoke with Rick Hall of ARD via phone. The contractor discovered during excavation a small hole in the buried 2" steel line, which was the result of the undetermined amount of fluids released on August 28, 2020. According to Mr. Hall, approximately 50 tons of impacted gravel/soil were removed during excavation on August 28, 2020. Impacted gravel/soils were placed on secondary containment stationed onsite and the materials were covered. Impacted gravel/soils were observed during my inspection. Water was observed on the secondary containment with field screenings ranging from 52.8 uS/cm- 65.1 uS/cm. The Department recommends removing the rain water from the secondary containment.After excavation and repairing a section of the 2" dump line, the operator opted to leave the trench open and staked off with orange safety fence. According to Mr. Hall, there are three pipe lines running in the same ditch line. The first is the 2" steel dump line located at approximately 2' 8" deep below the surface. A 3" steel discharge line located in the same ditch line and a 6" steel suction line located approximately 4 feet away from the 2" dump line and is approximately 5' 8" below the surface. Mr. Hall stated that a bed of sand is located beneath the 6" suction line and conductivity readings were elevated in sections of that sand. Tuscarora Geological & Environmental Services collected samples from the impacted sand area. Mr. Hall requested that the sample results be expedited. Samples results are pending.While I was onsite I viewed the open trench. I screened throughout the 2" dump line side of the trench and readings ranged from 0.100 mS/cm to 0.300 mS/cm. I screened on the 6" suction line side of the trench and I was getting elevated readings >4.00 mS/cm in an approximate 2' diameter area. These elevated readings were adjacent to where the 2" dump line was repaired. As I moved away from that 2' diameter area, screenings dropped to 0.100 mS/cm to 0.400 mS/cm.No new violations have been cited. Outstanding violations remain.

Comments: The weather was 73 degrees and sunny at the time of this inspection. The above-referenced gas well is currently listed as Active in eFACTS. The purpose of this inspection is to evaluate well integrity at the end of a 72-hour pressure build-up test. Six(6) Unconventional gas wells have been spud on the Pad. At the conclusion of testing at the above-referenced well, pressures were measured with a crystal pressure gauge and recorded prior to opening each annulus vent. Each annulus vent was immediately checked for presence/absence of combustible gas using Creston's Bascom Turner GasExplorer meter (calibrated 8/27/2026). A gas sample was not collected from the 13 3/8" x 9 5/8" and 20" x 13 3/8" annulus vents. ¿¿ The area immediately surrounding the well head was also monitored for combustible gas using an Altair 5X combustible gas meter (calibrated 7/28/2026). The results of this monitoring indicated that 0% LEL and 0% Methane was measured during the inspection. Violations are continued from original date of 5/01/2025. No new violations were noted at this inspection.
